title: Lyapunov stability
physicalPurpose: Stabilize the upright pendulum while distinguishing mathematically certified initial states from simulated recoveries.
objective: Prove a local nonlinear stability region.

simplifications: The rigid pendulum omits motor electrical dynamics, gearbox compliance, encoder quantization, pivot friction, structural flexibility and external disturbances.
The exact configured nonlinear sine-gravity model is Simulation truth, not an identified physical rig.
The quadratic certificate proves only the declared sublevel set and unsaturated feedback assumptions.
A finite phase-plane trajectory map validates examples but does not prove a global region of attraction.

baseline.limitation: One successful nonlinear trajectory does not establish an invariant region or prove convergence for neighbouring initial states.

change.decision: Call an initial state certified only when it lies in the declared sublevel set and all model, feedback, torque and decrease assumptions remain valid.

disturbances: Repeat the unchanged nonlinear rig and controller from the declared certified initial-state map.
Repeat from plus and minus 0.25 rad outside the sublevel set without promoting recovery to certificate evidence.
Repeat from 0.8 rad to expose requested/applied torque separation and certificate rejection under saturation.

acceptance.window: all samples of every declared certified trajectory
initialized non-equilibrium samples of every certified trajectory

abortPredicates: Any required angle, rate, torque, certificate or evidence signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, invalid, missing or bound incorrectly.
The model, equilibrium, interval, initial state, feedback gain, torque limit, P matrix or certificate level differs from the declared record.
A certified trajectory leaves the sublevel set, saturates, or has nonnegative continuous derivative or positive sampled change away from equilibrium.
An outside simulated recovery is labelled as certified or global evidence.
safety.restorationMode: Disable feedback and verify exactly zero applied motor torque before restoring the upright simulated state.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised controls engineer with laboratory, mechanical, electrical and machine-safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: No physical pendulum, motor or laboratory rig is operated.
The configured sine-gravity dynamics and all trajectories are Simulation evidence.
Physical use requires an identified model, guarding, independent emergency stop, reviewed torque topology, explicit immediate approval and rollback.

video.viewerOutcome: Distinguish a local nonlinear stability certificate from a successful simulated pendulum trajectory.

learning.context: A torque motor must balance a rigid pendulum at its physically unstable upright orientation.
learning.reason: One successful nonlinear recovery cannot prove an invariant attraction region or justify a global stability claim.
theory: A phase plane shows angle-error and angular-rate trajectories from different initial states.
A positive Lyapunov function with negative derivative can certify a declared invariant sublevel set.
The nonlinear sine remainder, torque limit and sampling assumptions remain part of the claim.
Simulation outside a certified set is observation, not mathematical proof.
learning.workedPrediction: At 0.1 rad error and zero rate, predict -0.4 N m requested torque, V 0.0066667 and V_dot about -0.0050028; at 0.25 rad predict V 0.0416667 outside rho 0.025.
practicalPreparation: Verify the upright equilibrium, nonlinear model, controller and plant intervals, feedback gains, torque limit, P matrix, rho and Simulation class.
Calculate both worked initial-state classifications before running the phase trajectories.
learning.baseline: Observe one nonlinear recovery and state why that trace alone cannot establish a region of attraction.
learning.change: Evaluate the declared Lyapunov certificate over the complete inside and outside initial-state map without changing feedback.
learning.comparison: Compare phase trajectories, V, V_dot, sampled change, torque, saturation, sublevel membership and final state under equivalent conditions.
learning.validation: Prove nonlinear RK4 agreement, invariant decrease for every certified case, explicit rejection outside the set and under saturation, and zero disabled torque.
learning.explanation: Negative derivative makes the declared sublevel set invariant; a recovered outside trajectory does not enlarge the proven set.
